page: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v4 is a constrained-vCPU memory-optimized virtual machine hosted via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, with 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial, offering 128.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 16.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 275 GB of local SSD temporary storage, while hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not present. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark results demonstrate intermediate general-purpose throughput paired with lower stress-testing capacity. General processing tests report average performance across multiple workloads, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1604.0, a multi-core score of 6375.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 11895.86. The instance achieves 8.29 million operations per second on Redis SET operations, 10.12 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and single-threaded gzip compression of 26.77 GB/sec. However, raw compute density is restricted, with stress-ng recording 763.78 in single-core and 3060.15 in multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth reaches 515.14 GB/sec for small cached reads, falling to 39.27 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 22.62 GB/sec for large writes. Machine learning workloads on 7B parameter models remain low due to CPU-only execution, producing 15.36 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 6.29 tokens/sec for generation.

The constrained configuration of the E16-8as_v4 reduces core count while retaining the 128.0 GB memory footprint of a standard 16-vCPU instance. This design optimizes licensing expenditure for software packages charged on a per-core basis, while preserving high memory availability. Tradeoffs include lower multi-threaded throughput and reduced uncached memory bandwidth compared to unconstrained platforms. Suitable workloads include relational database management systems, in-memory caches such as Redis, enterprise resource planning applications, and intermediate data processing workflows that require large memory pools without high core density.

It delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs over 4 physical cores alongside 128.0 GB of memory, resulting in a high 16.0 GB per core ratio. The instance includes 275 GB of local SSD temporary storage and no dedicated GPUs.
